event_title: Athens-Clarke passes emergency data center moratorium
event_description: Commission unanimously approved temporary emergency moratorium until March 6, 2026 following denial of 2M sf proposal. 25-year-old zoning code lacks data center definition.

event_title: Coweta County extends moratorium to December 17
event_description: Board signed resolution extending 180-day moratorium to earliest of December 17, 2025 or adoption of land use amendments. Project Sail remains pending.

event_title: $1.2B Project Turbo withdrawn from Hall County
event_description: Developer withdrew special use permit application citing 'insufficient fact-finding' at commission level. Gainesville confirmed inadequate water capacity for project.

event_title: Georgia DCA approves new data center DRI thresholds
event_description: Board unanimously approved 'technological facilities' category: 500,000 sf outside Atlanta, 300,000 sf in metro areas triggers Development of Regional Impact review.

event_title: Dermody PL data center approved in Social Circle
event_description: City Council approved four 250,000 sf buildings plus 100,000 sf substation on 96 acres. First building 2-3 years; full build-out 5 years.

event_title: Jones County rescinds data center ordinance due to legal issues
event_description: County rescinded strict zoning ordinances adopted in September due to legal concerns about procedural requirements.

event_title: Monroe County passes data center moratorium
event_description: 4-1 vote establishing moratorium until March 2026 commission meeting. Does not apply to City of Forsyth projects. 'Groton solution' under consideration.

event_title: Atlas Development approved despite Planning denial
event_description: Social Circle City Council overrode Planning Commission's unanimous denial with 2-1 vote for 1.5M sf, 288 MW data center. Nearly 100 people attended.

event_title: Google purchases 948 acres in Monroe County
event_description: Google closed on $42.6M purchase of land at Rumble Road adjacent to approved Rumble Technology Campus for future data center development.

event_title: Twiggs County approves 900 MW Pine Ridge Tech Park
event_description: Commission unanimously approved rezoning for 291-acre hyperscale facility with power demand equal to Macon plus Augusta. Decision 'met with boos and applause.'

event_title: Social Circle enacts 90-day data center moratorium
event_description: City unanimously passed moratorium to 'work through data center requests already in hand.' City Manager: 'It's coming too fast, too soon.'

event_title: Jones County adopts strict data center ordinance
event_description: Requirements include closed-loop cooling, crypto mining ban, 45/35 dB noise limits, 100-ft buffers, HVAC concealment. Later rescinded November 2025 due to legal issues.

event_title: LaGrange approves 180-day data center moratorium
event_description: Project Pegasus unaffected (permits already approved). 150 parcels currently allow data centers with no specific UDO regulations.

event_title: Troup County passes 90-day moratorium
event_description: Covers unincorporated county only. 200+ attendees at September 4 town hall. Extended to coordinate with LaGrange's 180-day moratorium.

event_title: Clayton County approves 120-day data center moratorium
event_description: Resolution 2025-193 passed unanimously through December 31, 2025. Sponsored by Vice Chair Alaina Reaves to study environmental impacts.

event_title: Pike County passes data center moratorium
event_description: Commissioner Jenkins: 'People just don't understand data centers, yet.' County developing ordinance with second reading December 2025.

event_title: Lamar County passes moratorium for code updates
event_description: First county code update since 2010. Amazon had already purchased 985 acres for $270M before moratorium enacted.

event_title: Monroe County unanimously rejects Bolingbroke Tech Center
event_description: 900+ red-shirted residents packed meeting. $5.8B, 900-acre project denied unanimously. Landowners filed lawsuit alleging violation of zoning procedures.

event_title: Amazon purchases 985 acres in Lamar County for $270M
event_description: Part of Legacy 75 Trade Center. County rezoning approved August 4, 2025. $274K/acre—6x Monroe County prices for comparable land.

event_title: DeKalb County passes initial 100-day moratorium
event_description: 4-3 vote approving 100-day pause on data center applications. Later extended to December 16, 2025 with 6-0 vote.

event_title: $19B Project Bunkhouse approved with conditions
event_description: Planning Commission recommended approval of 8.6M sf, 12-building campus on 876 acres. Development Authority declined to offer incentives.

event_title: Atlanta requires special-use permits for data centers
event_description: Bans data centers in Little Five Points, East Atlanta Village, Inman Park, Virginia-Highlands, Cascade Heights. 150K sf/floor limits elsewhere.

event_title: Bartow Planning Commission recommends denial of Springbank
event_description: $4.5B Atlas Development project near Barnsley Resort denied. ~1,700 petition signatures; concerns about tourism jobs. 'Good idea, wrong location.'

event_title: Coweta County passes 180-day moratorium
event_description: Unanimous vote triggered by Project Sail ($17B) filing. Citizens for Rural Coweta collected 1,750 petition signatures opposing development.

event_title: Project Peach approved 3-2 despite opposition
event_description: $1B, 2.1M sf data center approved with 27 conditions. Palmetto Mayor Teresa Thomas-Smith opposed the project.

event_title: First data center approved in Henry County
event_description: 5-0 vote for Southeast Property Holdings 133-acre, three-building campus off GA-20. Part of Henderson Farms development.

event_title: Douglas County passes 90-day moratorium
event_description: 4-1 vote despite county being 'birthplace of Georgia data centers.' Commissioner Raxton: opportunity to align with comprehensive plan.

event_title: Bartow County adopts data center ordinance
event_description: 200-ft buffers from residential, 65/55 dB noise limits. Administrator: 'We're pro data center here.'

event_title: Amazon announces $11B Georgia investment
event_description: Largest corporate announcement in Georgia history. Split between Butts and Douglas counties. 550+ high-skilled jobs expected.

event_title: Sailfish Investors annexation approved
event_description: Walton County commissioners approved annexation for $1.7B, 1.78M sf data center to be developed by Sailfish Investors.

event_title: DeKalb extends moratorium to December 16, 2025
event_description: 6-0 vote to extend initial 100-day moratorium. Staff directed to develop tiered ordinance with Minor/Medium/Major/Campus categories.

event_title: Atlanta bans data centers near BeltLine
event_description: City Council voted unanimously to prohibit data centers within 22-mile BeltLine overlay and half-mile of MARTA rail stations.

event_title: Switch files DRI for $772M second Georgia campus
event_description: KEEP 2.0 Atlanta North Campus on 126 acres. 1,200 MW commitment via Georgia EMC. Phase 1 expected Q2 2026.

event_title: T5 acquires 91-acre site in South Fulton
event_description: 1.32M sf, 200 MW campus planned. Substation operational 2026, Phase 1 delivery 2027.

event_title: QTS Fayetteville construction progresses
event_description: 615-acre, 7M sf, 250+ MW campus under construction. Microsoft Fairwater AI superfactory to be first tenant.

event_title: DC BLOX announces Rockdale County campus
event_description: DC BLOX set to build hyperscale-ready campus. 72 acres near Conyers with 216 MW committed by Georgia Power. Phase 1 Q4 2025.

event_title: White Oak Technology Park DRI Filed with State
event_description: Trammell Crow Co., a subsidiary of commercial real estate giant CBRE, filed a Development of Regional Impact (DRI) application with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for the White Oak Technology Park. The proposal includes 29 data center buildings totaling 8 million square feet on 1,945 acres near Morris Callaway Road and Innovation Parkway. The estimated build-out value is $11.6 billion with projected annual tax revenue exceeding $118 million.

event_title: Planning Commission Approves S-1 Rezoning for Data Center Site
event_description: The Columbia County Planning Commission unanimously approved a request from the Economic Development Authority of Columbia County to rezone 1,945 acres behind White Oak Business Park from residential-agricultural to S-1 (Special Use) zoning. This rezoning enables data center, research and development, and cybersecurity uses on the property.

event_title: Development Authority Launches Public Information Website for Data Center Project
event_description: The Economic Development Authority of Columbia County launched a new website to provide public information about the White Oak Technology Park project. Executive Director Cheney Eldridge stated the site aims to address resident concerns about water usage, power infrastructure, and environmental impacts, emphasizing transparency without advocating for any particular position.

event_title: Appling Residents Voice Opposition to Data Center Plans
event_description: Residents near the proposed White Oak Technology Park site expressed concerns about the project, claiming they were not adequately informed about the plans. Resident Alan Wyatt stated he discovered the project encompasses 3 square miles of industrial development. Concerns included noise, water usage, and impacts on rural character. Some residents met with commissioners who indicated the development could reduce property taxes.

event_title: PSC Commissioner Discusses Data Center at Campaign Stop
event_description: Georgia Public Service Commissioner Tim Echols made a campaign stop in Columbia County where the proposed data center became the main topic of discussion. Echols expressed support for the project's potential revenue benefits while acknowledging resident concerns. Some attendees remained on the fence, requesting more information about impacts from communities with existing data centers.

event_title: Planning Commission Recommends Data Center Zoning District to Board
event_description: The Columbia County Planning Commission voted to recommend approval of a text amendment creating a new DC (Data Center) zoning district. The proposed ordinance includes a 70-decibel noise limit, 500-foot buffers from residential properties, and restrictions on generator testing. Approximately 15 residents spoke during public comment, most opposing the new district. The ordinance was forwarded to the Board of Commissioners.

event_title: Board of Commissioners Holds First Reading of DC Zoning Ordinance
event_description: Columbia County commissioners conducted the first reading of the proposed data center zoning ordinance following months of public debate. The proposed guidelines establish 75-foot maximum building height, 500-foot natural buffers from residential properties, and 70-decibel noise limits. Despite resident concerns about noise and water usage, commissioners unanimously approved moving the proposal to final reading on December 2.

event_title: Georgia Power Approves Power Consumption Model for White Oak Project
event_description: Chairman Douglas Duncan announced that Georgia Power has approved the proposed power consumption model for the White Oak Technology Park data center project. This approval brings the county closer to securing an end user for the project. Duncan stated that all infrastructure and utility costs will be borne by the end user with no financial burden on residents. Land acquisition is anticipated to complete before December 19.

event_title: Data Center Zoning Ordinance Passed on Second Reading
event_description: The Columbia County Board of Commissioners approved Ordinance No. 25-07 on second reading, formally establishing the DC (Data Center) zoning district. The ordinance amends Chapter 90 of county code with provisions for buffer requirements, screening rules, and noise limits. Residents continued to voice concerns about the 70-decibel limit and water consumption during public comment. Requests to pause for independent impact studies were not adopted.

event_title: County Officials Discuss Data Center Zoning Preparedness
event_description: Macon-Bibb County Planning and Zoning Executive Director Jeff Ruggieri confirmed that while no formal data center applications have been received, the county's existing zoning code can handle such proposals. Data centers would be classified as heavy industrial use requiring conditional use permits. Mayor Lester Miller stated he would only support data centers in commercial areas away from residential neighborhoods, citing concerns about other counties' experiences with data center impacts.
